data.why: The app's primary data path is a built-in synthetic NIR-like spectral generator (sample_data.py) selectable in the sidebar, so no example file is strictly required; a small hand-written PFAS congener panel CSV (with one missing value and one injected outlier row) is provided to exercise the alternate 'Upload CSV' path and the app's missing-value and outlier-flagging logic.

goals: Explore the structure of an analytical dataset using PCA (scree, score, and loading plots) to see how samples and features relate
Detect multivariate outliers via Hotelling's T2 and Q-residual control limits and flag samples needing analyst review
Compare preprocessing methods (autoscale, SNV, MSC, Savitzky-Golay) to see how they affect PCA structure and outlier detection
Fit a PLS regression model to predict a quantitative target (e.g., a PFAS concentration) from feature columns and evaluate RMSE/MAE/R2 via train/test split and cross-validation
Rank features by standardized PLS coefficient influence to interpret which analytical variables drive the prediction
Assess applicability domain (Mahalanobis distance, leverage) and per-sample prediction uncertainty to decide which predictions are trustworthy

review.summary: The tree captures the README's workflow well: load, PCA explore, T²/Q flagging, cross-validated PLS, feature influence, applicability domain and export. Its labels are clean, and the evidence I opened matches in almost every case. It needs small fixes before filing: correct the wrong 'diamonds' claim, put preprocessing where it belongs, drop the About phase, split f10, and surface the suspicious Q-limit counts.
